title: Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data During Transmission
description: Parent registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) transmitted from ExternalEntity EE1 to Process P1 may be intercepted by network attackers or eavesdroppers during the flow.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without adequate encryption or authentication mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 from context as it applies to ExternalEntity->Process flows; tree_node may need verification against full LINDDUN Pro methodology.

title: Identification of Parent User via Government ID and Email
description: Government ID and email address in registration data can be used to uniquely identify the parent user, potentially enabling profiling or targeted attacks.
assumptions: Government ID and email are unique identifiers that can be correlated with other data sources.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as representative identification threat for ExternalEntity->Process flow; tree_node may need verification.

title: Usurpation/Impersonation via Stolen Credentials
description: Password and government ID combination could enable an attacker to impersonate the parent user if credentials are compromised during registration flow.
assumptions: Password and government ID are sufficient for authentication and identity verification.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as representative usurpation threat; tree_node may need verification against full LINDDUN Pro methodology.

title: Disclosure of Registration Data by Authentication Service
description: Authentication Service P1 may improperly store, log, or share parent registration data (especially password and government ID) with unauthorized parties or through inadequate access controls.
assumptions: Authentication service has inadequate data protection measures, logging practices, or access controls.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as representative disclosure threat for Process element; tree_node may need verification.

title: Data Alteration of Registration Information
description: Authentication Service P1 may alter parent registration data (email, name, government ID) during processing, leading to identity fraud or incorrect user profiles.
assumptions: Authentication service lacks proper data integrity controls, audit logging, or input validation.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as representative data alteration threat; tree_node may need verification.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure of Parent Account Information
description: The authentication service stores parent account information in MongoDB, creating an explicit disclosure of personal data. If access controls are inadequate, this data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Parent account information contains personally identifiable information that is not strictly necessary for the authentication service's core function.
uncertainty_note: Assuming parent account data is PII and access controls may be insufficient

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Stored Parent Account Data
description: The MongoDB users collection storing parent account information could be tampered with by unauthorized actors, leading to data integrity violations and potential account manipulation.
assumptions: MongoDB collection lacks adequate integrity controls or is accessible without proper authentication.
uncertainty_note: Assuming MongoDB may not have sufficient integrity controls

title: Identification of Users via Parent Account Data
description: Parent account information stored in the authentication service could be used to identify individuals, potentially enabling profiling or tracking across systems.
assumptions: Parent account data is unique enough to identify individuals and could be correlated with other data sources.
uncertainty_note: Assuming parent account data has identification value

title: User Identifiability via JWT Token
description: The JWT token transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Parent User contains user data that can directly identify the user. This creates a privacy risk as the user's identity is exposed in the token payload.
assumptions: JWT token contains personally identifiable information (PII) or user attributes that can be used to identify the user.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure to Parent User
description: User data transmitted via JWT may be disclosed to the Parent User without proper authorization or consent. The Parent User may not have legitimate access rights to this sensitive information.
assumptions: Parent User may not have proper authorization to receive this user data.

title: JWT Token Usurpation/Impersonation Risk
description: The JWT token containing user data could be intercepted or misused by unauthorized parties, allowing them to impersonate the user or gain unauthorized access to systems that trust this token.
assumptions: JWT token is transmitted over a channel that could be intercepted or is not properly secured.

title: Child login linked to parent identity
description: Child's authentication using parent email creates linkability between child's activities and parent's identity, potentially exposing child's behavior patterns to parent or third parties who can access parent's data.
assumptions: Parent email is unique identifier that can be linked to parent's account
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific child-parent linking may require more granular node selection.

title: Child identifiable via parent email
description: Child's login reveals parent email, making child identifiable as a dependent of that parent, potentially exposing family relationships and enabling profiling of child's activities.
assumptions: Parent email is stored/transmitted during authentication
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is general identifiability; specific family relationship exposure may need more specific node.

title: Parent credentials disclosed during transmission
description: Parent email and password transmitted during child login could be intercepted or logged, exposing parent's authentication credentials to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Credentials transmitted over network during authentication flow
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is general disclosure; specific credential exposure may need more granular node.

title: Child identity usurpation via parent credentials
description: Third party with access to parent credentials could potentially usurp child's identity by using parent email to authenticate as child, bypassing child-specific access controls.
assumptions: Parent credentials are accessible to unauthorized parties
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is general usurpation; specific child identity usurpation may need more specific node.

title: Linkability of Child Identity Across Systems
description: The JWT token and child profiles transmitted from the Authentication Service could be linked to identify the child user across different services or contexts, potentially enabling cross-service tracking and profiling.
assumptions: The JWT and profile data contain unique identifiers that can be correlated across systems.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific child profile context may warrant more granular analysis.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile information transmitted via the authentication flow could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or at the receiving endpoint, violating child privacy protections.
assumptions: The transmission channel or receiving endpoint may lack adequate access controls.
uncertainty_note: Severity elevated due to child data sensitivity; actual risk depends on encryption and endpoint security.

title: Authentication Token Misuse for Identity Usurpation
description: The JWT token could be intercepted or misused by unauthorized actors to impersonate the child user, gaining access to services or data under the child's identity.
assumptions: JWT tokens may be transmitted or stored insecurely, enabling token theft or replay attacks.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a general usurpation node; specific JWT token lifecycle details would refine this assessment.

title: Linking of child profile data to other datasets
description: The child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) contains identifiers that can be used to link this profile to other datasets, potentially creating a comprehensive profile of the child across systems.
assumptions: Other systems or databases exist that contain overlapping data about this child or family members.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 from context [3] as it covers ExternalEntity→Process interactions

title: Identification of child through government ID
description: The government ID is a unique identifier that directly identifies the child. Combined with name and DOB, this creates a strong identification risk where the child can be uniquely identified across systems.
assumptions: The government ID is stored and potentially accessible to authorized or unauthorized parties.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as it covers identification threats at source position

title: Disclosure of sensitive government ID information
description: The government ID is highly sensitive personal information. If this data is disclosed to unauthorized parties, it could lead to identity theft, fraud, or other privacy violations for the child.
assumptions: The data flow or storage mechanisms are not adequately protected against unauthorized access.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as it covers disclosure threats at source position

title: Disclosure of child profile to third parties
description: The child's profile data could be disclosed to third parties (e.g., service providers, partners, or malicious actors) without proper consent or legal basis, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: The system may share data with third parties for business or operational purposes.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as it covers disclosure-to-third-party threats at source position

title: Understanding of child's identity and characteristics
description: The collected data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) enables understanding of the child's identity, demographics, and potentially other characteristics if linked with additional data sources.
assumptions: The data is accessible to system operators or authorized personnel who can analyze the profile.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as it covers understanding threats at source position

title: Unintended child profile data disclosure during storage
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB may be inadvertently disclosed through improper access controls, logging, or backup mechanisms. The minimality principle requires that only strictly necessary personal data be stored.
assumptions: MongoDB collection may have insufficient access controls or logging may expose sensitive child data
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as it relates to data disclosure during storage operations

title: Child profile data remains identifiable after storage
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB collection contains personally identifiable information that could be used to identify the child, potentially violating privacy expectations for minors.
assumptions: Child profiles contain direct identifiers (name, DOB, contact info) that make data identifiable
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 selected as it addresses identifiability of stored personal data

title: Child profile data integrity compromised during storage
description: Child profile data could be tampered with or corrupted during the store/update process in MongoDB, leading to inaccurate or fraudulent child information.
assumptions: Insufficient validation or encryption during data storage operations
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 addresses data integrity threats during storage operations

title: Child profile data linkable to other data sources
description: Stored child profile data could be linked with other datasets (e.g., medical records, school records, parental data) creating comprehensive profiles that exceed intended privacy boundaries.
assumptions: MongoDB may be queried alongside other systems or data may be exported for cross-referencing
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 addresses linkability risks when data is stored and potentially accessed across systems

title: Linkability of video search results to user identity
description: Video search results and user interactions (likes, comments) may be linked to the specific child user (EE2) through account associations, creating a profile of viewing behavior and preferences.
assumptions: System maintains user accounts and links search activity to user profiles

title: Identifiability through video content and comments
description: Video content viewed, liked, or commented on may contain personally identifiable information or reveal sensitive information about the child user's interests, location, or associations.
assumptions: Video content may contain metadata or visible PII; comments may reveal personal information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video content
description: Video content accessed through the search and request functionality may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data leakage.
assumptions: Video content is stored and transmitted; access controls may be insufficient

title: Improper personal data management in video content
description: The Video Management Service (P2) may improperly manage personal data contained in video content, including retention, deletion, or sharing practices that violate privacy regulations or user expectations.
assumptions: Service stores video content and user interaction data; data management policies may be inadequate
uncertainty_note: Context [5] confirms Nc.2 applies to data management risks with privacy outcomes

title: Identifying information in video metadata
description: Video metadata (e.g., timestamps, locations, device IDs, user IDs) may contain personally identifiable information that can be used to identify individuals.
assumptions: Metadata fields may include user identifiers, timestamps, or location data that can be linked to specific individuals.
uncertainty_note: Context [3] supports I.1.2 for metadata identification, but specific metadata schema not fully known.

title: Unintended disclosure of video content
description: Video files stored in MongoDB may contain personal data (e.g., surveillance footage, user recordings) that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through access control failures or data breaches.
assumptions: Video content may capture identifiable individuals; access controls may not be properly enforced.
uncertainty_note: Context [4] supports Dd for data disclosure, but specific video content types not fully specified.

title: Linkability of video metadata across systems
description: Video metadata may be linkable across different systems or time periods, enabling tracking of individuals or activities through metadata correlation.
assumptions: Metadata may contain consistent identifiers (e.g., user IDs, device IDs) that can be correlated across systems.
uncertainty_note: Standard LINDDUN threat tree node L.1.1 used for linkability; specific metadata schema not fully known.

title: Child Identifiability from Search/Watch History
description: Search and watch history data stored in child profiles can reveal identifiable information about the child's interests, behaviors, and potentially location patterns, making the child identifiable even without direct PII.
assumptions: Search and watch history contains patterns that can be correlated with the child's identity or used to infer sensitive information about the child.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for identifiability threats; applied based on context of child data sensitivity.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure of Child Activity History
description: Child search and watch history may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or unintended sharing mechanisms, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: Data disclosure occurs when data is transferred across boundaries without proper authorization or when access controls are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for data disclosure; applied based on context of sensitive child data storage.

title: Tampering with Child Activity Records
description: Search and watch history data could be altered, deleted, or corrupted, compromising the integrity of the child's activity records and potentially affecting parental oversight or legal accountability.
assumptions: Data integrity threats occur when data is modified without authorization, affecting its accuracy and reliability.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for data integrity; applied based on context of stored activity data.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data Storage
description: Storing child search and watch history may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other child privacy regulations if data retention, consent, or minimality requirements are not properly implemented.
assumptions: Child data is subject to stricter regulatory requirements than adult data, including consent, minimality, and retention limits.
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for non-compliance; applied based on context of child data and regulatory obligations.

title: Video data linkability across systems
description: Uploaded video data may be linked to the user across different systems or contexts, enabling correlation of activities and identity tracking beyond the immediate video management service.
assumptions: Video metadata or content contains identifiers that can be used to link to other data sources.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a representative linkability node; specific tree node may vary based on full LINDDUN Pro taxonomy.

title: Video content reveals user identity
description: Video content may contain personally identifiable information (PII) that directly or indirectly identifies the user, such as facial features, location data, or contextual information.
assumptions: Video content is not adequately anonymized or blurred before processing.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a representative identifiability node; specific tree node may vary based on full LINDDUN Pro taxonomy.

title: Unauthorized video data disclosure
description: Video data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or inadequate encryption during transmission and storage.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or enforced.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a representative disclosure node; specific tree node may vary based on full LINDDUN Pro taxonomy.

title: Improper personal data management
description: Video data may be managed in non-compliance with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA), leading to legal and reputational risks.
assumptions: Data retention, consent, and processing practices do not fully comply with regulatory requirements.
uncertainty_note: Nc.2 (Improper personal data management) is from retrieved context [5] and directly applies to this flow.

title: Video stream disclosure to unauthorized parties
description: The video stream transmitted from the Video Management Service to the child user could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized third parties during transmission or storage.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a representative disclosure threat node; exact tree_node may vary based on full LINDDUN Pro taxonomy.

title: Child user identifiability from video content
description: The video stream contains biometric and behavioral data that can identify the child user, creating identifiability risks even if the video is 'approved'.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a representative identifiability threat node; exact tree_node may vary based on full LINDDUN Pro taxonomy.

title: Non-compliant video data management
description: The video data may not be managed in compliance with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., retention policies, access controls, consent requirements) during transmission to the child user.
uncertainty_note: Nc.2 'Improper personal data management' from retrieved context [5] is applicable to this flow.

title: Video stream linkability to other personal data
description: The video stream could be linked to other personal data about the child user (e.g., location, activity logs, other records), creating a comprehensive privacy profile.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a representative linkability threat node; exact tree_node may vary based on full LINDDUN Pro taxonomy.

title: Explicit disclosure of child browsing data to AI engine
description: Child browsing data is explicitly transferred from MongoDB childprofiles collection to AI Recommendation Engine as part of planned functionality. This represents intentional disclosure of personal data (children's data is highly sensitive) across a system boundary.
assumptions: The AI engine is a separate system component that processes this data, and the transfer is by design.
uncertainty_note: Citation based on context [5] regarding Dd threats and DataStore->Process mapping from context [3].

title: Identifiability of child data through browsing patterns
description: Child browsing data may contain identifiable information or patterns that could be used to identify the child, especially when combined with other data sources processed by the AI engine.
assumptions: Browsing data can contain quasi-identifiers that, when combined, could identify the child.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 inferred from LINDDUN methodology; context [3] confirms I threat type applies to DataStore->Process flows.

title: Linkability of child data across systems
description: Child browsing data transferred to AI engine could be linked with other data held by the AI system or external parties, creating a comprehensive profile of the child's behavior and preferences.
assumptions: The AI engine may have access to or share data with other systems, enabling cross-referencing.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 inferred from LINDDUN methodology; context [3] confirms L threat type applies to DataStore->Process flows.

title: Non-compliance with children's data protection regulations
description: Transfer of child browsing data to AI engine may violate regulations such as COPPA (US), GDPR-K (EU), or other children's privacy laws that impose strict requirements on data collection, processing, and disclosure for minors.
assumptions: The system operates under jurisdictions with children's data protection laws; the data transfer may not have proper consent or legal basis.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nc.1.1 inferred from LINDDUN methodology; context [3] confirms Nc threat type applies to DataStore->Process flows.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (P4) explicitly transfers browsing data to Third-Party Advertisers (EE3) by design. This is an intentional disclosure of personal data across a system boundary, which may violate the minimality principle if the data shared exceeds what is strictly necessary for the advertising purpose.
assumptions: Browsing data contains personal information that can be linked to individuals

title: Linkability of Browsing Data with Advertiser Profiles
description: Third-Party Advertisers (EE3) may link the received browsing data with other data they collect from users across different platforms, creating comprehensive user profiles that exceed the original purpose of the data transfer.
assumptions: Advertisers have access to multiple data sources and can correlate browsing behavior with other user activities

title: Identification of Individuals from Browsing Data
description: The browsing data transferred to advertisers may contain or enable identification of specific individuals, especially when combined with other data sources held by the advertisers.
assumptions: Browsing data includes identifiers or quasi-identifiers that can be used to identify individuals

title: Potential Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Transferring browsing data to third-party advertisers without adequate user consent or legal basis may violate privacy regulations such as GDPR, CCPA, or other applicable data protection laws.
assumptions: The data transfer lacks proper legal basis or user consent mechanisms
uncertainty_note: Assumes the organization has not implemented proper consent management for third-party data sharing

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Government ID Images
description: Government ID images stored in the file system could be accessed by unauthorized parties through vulnerabilities in the authentication service or file system access controls, leading to data disclosure.
assumptions: The authentication service and file system have access controls that could be bypassed or are insufficiently secure.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on context about data disclosure across boundaries; this is a reasonable fit for storage of sensitive personal data.

title: Tampering with Stored Government ID Images
description: Stored government ID images could be modified or corrupted by unauthorized actors, compromising data integrity and potentially enabling identity fraud.
assumptions: The file system lacks adequate integrity controls or the authentication service does not properly validate data before storage.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard node for data integrity threats in Process→DataStore flows.

title: Linkability of Stored ID Images to Other Data
description: Stored government ID images could be linked to other personal data or system logs, enabling profiling or correlation attacks that reveal additional information about data subjects.
assumptions: The stored images contain metadata or can be correlated with other data sources in the system.
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 is a standard node for linkability threats; this applies when stored data can be correlated with other data sources.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored JWT
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage are accessible to any JavaScript running in the browser, making them vulnerable to XSS attacks and unauthorized reading by malicious scripts.
assumptions: Attacker can execute JavaScript in the victim's browser

title: JWT Token Manipulation
description: localStorage is writable by any JavaScript code, allowing attackers to modify, delete, or inject malicious code into the stored JWT token.
assumptions: Attacker can execute JavaScript in the victim's browser

title: Linkability of User Sessions
description: JWT tokens contain user identifiers and session information that can be linked across different services or time periods, enabling user tracking and profiling.
assumptions: JWT contains identifiable user information

title: User Identification via Stored Token
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage can be used to identify and track specific users across sessions and potentially across different services if the token is shared.
assumptions: JWT contains user-identifying claims

title: Linking of child history data to build profile
description: Child history data retrieved for parent review may contain multiple data elements that can be linked together (e.g., dates, events, behaviors) to build a comprehensive profile of the child, potentially revealing sensitive information beyond what was intended to be shared.
assumptions: The child history contains multiple data points that can be correlated; the parent has access to all retrieved data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 chosen based on general linking methodology; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child history to parent
description: Child history data may be disclosed to the parent user without proper authorization or beyond the scope of intended parental review, potentially violating child privacy rights or data protection regulations.
assumptions: The system may not properly validate parental authorization; data may be accessible to unauthorized parties.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 chosen based on general disclosure methodology; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Parent misunderstanding of child history data
description: The parent user may misinterpret or misunderstand the child history data retrieved, leading to incorrect conclusions about the child's development, behavior, or needs.
assumptions: The data may be presented without adequate context or explanation; the parent may lack expertise to interpret the data correctly.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 chosen based on general understanding methodology; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.
